title.zh: 卷九十三 晉書19: 列傳八 盧質 李專美 盧詹 崔梲 薛融 曹國珍 張仁愿 趙熙 李遐 尹玉羽 鄭雲叟
title.en: Volume 93 Book of Later Jin 19: Biographies 8: Lu Zhi, Li Zhuanmei, Lu Zhan, Cui Zhuo, Xue Rong, Cao Guozhen, Zhang Renyuan, Zhao Xi, Li Xia, Yin Yuyu, Zheng Yunsou
title.raw: 卷九十三 晉書19: 列傳八 盧質 李專美 盧詹 崔梲 薛融 曹國珍 張仁愿 趙熙 李遐 尹玉羽 鄭雲叟 Volume 93 Book of Later Jin 19: Biographies 8: Lu Zhi, Li Zhuanmei, Lu Zhan, Cui Zhuo, Xue Rong, Cao Guozhen, Zhang Renyuan, Zhao Xi, Li Xia, Yin Yuyu, Zheng Yunsou

sentences.zh: 盧質，字子徵，河南人也。

translations.literal: Lu Zhi, courtesy name Zizheng, was a man of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Zhi, whose courtesy name was Zizheng, came from Henan.

sentences.zh: 曾祖偲，唐太原府祁縣尉，累贈右僕射。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Si was magistrate of Qi County in the Taiyuan prefecture of Tang, and was posthumously ennobled through successive promotions to Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Si had served as magistrate of Qi County in Taiyuan Prefecture under the Tang, and was posthumously promoted by successive honors to Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 祖衍，唐刑部侍郎、太子賓客，累贈太保。

translations.literal: His grandfather Yan was Vice Minister of Justice and Tutor to the Crown Prince under Tang, and was posthumously ennobled through successive promotions to Grand Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Yan had been Vice Minister of Justice and Tutor to the Crown Prince under the Tang, and was posthumously raised by successive honors to Grand Tutor.

sentences.zh: 父望，唐尚書司勛郎中，累贈太子少傅。

translations.literal: His father Wang was Director in the Bureau of Merits under the Ministry of Personnel of Tang, and was posthumously ennobled through successive promotions to Junior Tutor to the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: His father Wang had served as Director in the Bureau of Merits under the Tang Ministry of Personnel, and was posthumously promoted by successive honors to Junior Tutor to the Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 質幼聰慧，善屬文。

translations.literal: Zhi was clever from childhood and skilled at literary composition.
translations.idiomatic: From childhood Zhi was exceptionally bright and gifted at literary composition.

sentences.zh: 年十六，陜帥王重盈奏授芮城令，能以色養。

translations.literal: At age sixteen, Wang Chongying, military governor of Shaanxi, memorialized the throne to appoint him magistrate of Ruicheng; he was able to support his parents with cheerful countenance.
translations.idiomatic: At sixteen, Wang Chongying, military governor of Shaanxi, had him appointed magistrate of Ruicheng by imperial order, and he was able to support his parents with devoted filial care.

sentences.zh: 又為同州澄城令，從私便也。

translations.literal: He also served as magistrate of Chengcheng in Tong Prefecture, following his personal convenience.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as magistrate of Chengcheng in Tong Prefecture, a post chosen for his own convenience.

sentences.zh: 秩滿改秘書郎，丁母憂，歸河南故裏。

translations.literal: When his term expired he was made Secretary; upon his mother's death he returned to his old home in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: When his term ended he was appointed Secretary; after his mother's death he returned to his ancestral home in Henan.

sentences.zh: 天祐三年，北遊太原，時李襲吉在武皇幕府，以女妻之。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tianyou he traveled north to Taiyuan; at that time Li Xiji was on the staff of the Martial Emperor's headquarters and gave him his daughter in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Tianyou he went north to Taiyuan, where Li Xiji was then serving on the Martial Emperor's staff and gave him his daughter in marriage.

sentences.zh: 武皇憐其才，承制授檢校兵部郎中，充河東節度掌書記，賜緋魚袋。

translations.literal: The Martial Emperor cherished his talent and, by imperial commission, appointed him acting Director in the Bureau of Military Affairs, to serve as secretarial recorder for the Hedong military commission, and granted him the scarlet robe and fish tally.
translations.idiomatic: The Martial Emperor admired his talent and, acting by imperial commission, appointed him acting Director in the Bureau of Military Affairs and secretarial recorder for the Hedong military commission, granting him the scarlet robe and fish tally.

sentences.zh: 武皇厭代，其弟克寧握兵柄，有嗣襲之望，質與張承業等密謀，同立莊宗為嗣，有翊贊之功。

translations.literal: When the Martial Emperor passed away, his younger brother Kening held military power and harbored hopes of succeeding to the position; Zhi secretly plotted with Zhang Chengye and others to install Zhuangzong as heir together, and had the merit of assisting and supporting him.
translations.idiomatic: After the Martial Emperor's death his younger brother Kening held the army and hoped to succeed him, but Zhi joined Zhang Chengye and others in a secret plot to install Zhuangzong as heir, earning merit for his loyal support.

sentences.zh: 及莊宗四征，質皆從行。

translations.literal: When Zhuangzong undertook his four campaigns, Zhi accompanied him on all of them.
translations.idiomatic: On all four of Zhuangzong's major campaigns, Zhi accompanied the army.

sentences.zh: 十六年，轉節度判官、檢校禮部尚書。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he was transferred to military commission adjutant and acting Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year he was made adjutant of the military commission and acting Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 十九年，莊宗將即帝位，命為大禮使，累加至銀青光祿大夫、檢校右僕射。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year, as Zhuangzong was about to ascend the throne, he was appointed Director of Grand Ceremonies and was promoted in succession to Silver-Gleaming Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and acting Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year, as Zhuangzong prepared to take the throne, he was appointed Director of Grand Ceremonies and was promoted in succession to Silver-Gleaming Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and acting Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 二十年，授行臺禮部尚書。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year he was appointed Minister of Rites of the mobile imperial secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year he was appointed Minister of Rites of the mobile imperial secretariat.

sentences.zh: 莊宗既登極，欲相之，質性疏逸，不喜居高位，固辭獲免。

translations.literal: After Zhuangzong had ascended the throne he wished to make Zhi chief minister, but Zhi's nature was free and easy; he did not like holding high office and firmly declined, thereby being excused.
translations.idiomatic: Once Zhuangzong had taken the throne he wished to make Zhi chief minister, but Zhi was by nature easygoing and aloof and disliked high office; he firmly declined and was excused.

sentences.zh: 尋以本官兼太原尹，充北京留守事，未赴任，改戶部尚書、知制誥，充翰林學士承旨。

translations.literal: Soon thereafter, while retaining his original office, he was also made Governor of Taiyuan and charged with the duties of northern capital regent; before he took up the post he was changed to Minister of Revenue, Controller of Edicts, and Chief Academician of the Hanlin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was additionally appointed Governor of Taiyuan and charged as regent of the northern capital, but before he took up the post he was reassigned as Minister of Revenue, Controller of Edicts, and Chief Academician of the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 同光元年冬，從平大梁，權判租庸事，逾月隨駕都洛，旋受詔權知汴州軍府事。

translations.literal: In the winter of the first year of Tongguang he followed the campaign that pacified Daliang and was temporarily put in charge of the equal-tax and corvée administration; after more than a month he accompanied the imperial procession to Luoyang, and soon received an edict to act as temporary administrator of the Bianzhou military headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the first year of Tongguang he followed the conquest of Daliang and was temporarily placed in charge of equal-tax and corvée affairs; a month later he accompanied the court to Luoyang, and soon received orders to serve as acting administrator of the Bianzhou military headquarters.

sentences.zh: 時孔謙握利權，志在聚斂，累移文於汴，配民放絲，質堅論之，事雖不行，時論賞之。

translations.literal: At that time Kong Qian held financial power and aimed at accumulation; he repeatedly sent documents to Bian ordering the populace levied to deliver silk, and Zhi argued against it firmly; although the matter was not carried out, contemporary opinion praised him.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Kong Qian controlled the finances and was intent on squeezing revenue; he repeatedly sent orders to Bian requiring the people to be levied for silk deliveries. Zhi argued vigorously against this, and although his protest was not heeded, public opinion praised him.

sentences.zh: 俄又改金紫光祿大夫、兵部尚書、知制誥、翰林學士承旨，仍賜論思匡佐功臣。

translations.literal: Before long he was again changed to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon, Minister of War, Controller of Edicts, and Chief Academician of the Hanlin Academy, and was further granted the title of Meritorious Minister for Deliberation and Support.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was promoted to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon, Minister of War, Controller of Edicts, and Chief Academician of the Hanlin Academy, and was granted the title Meritorious Minister for Deliberation and Support.

sentences.zh: 會覆試進士，質以「後從諫則聖」為賦題，以「堯、舜、禹、湯傾心求過」為韻，舊例賦韻四平四側，質所出韻乃五平三側，由是大為識者所誚。

translations.literal: When the repeat examination for presented scholars was held, Zhi set the fu topic as "He who later follows remonstrance is sage" and the rhyme words as "Yao, Shun, Yu, and Tang bent their hearts to seek their faults"; by old precedent fu rhymes were four level tones and four oblique tones, but the rhymes Zhi produced were five level and three oblique, and on this account he was greatly ridiculed by the learned.
translations.idiomatic: When the repeat examination for presented scholars was held, Zhi set the fu topic "He who later follows remonstrance is sage" with the rhyme phrase "Yao, Shun, Yu, and Tang bent their hearts to seek their faults." By precedent fu rhymes required four level tones and four oblique tones, but Zhi's set had five level and three oblique, and learned opinion mocked him roundly for it.

sentences.zh: 天成元年，制授特進、檢校司空、同州節度使。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tiancheng, by imperial edict he was appointed Special Advancement, acting Minister of Works, and military governor of Tong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tiancheng he was appointed by edict Special Advancement, acting Minister of Works, and military governor of Tong Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 時宰相馮道以詩餞別，其警句云：「視草北來唐學士，擁旄西去漢將軍。」

translations.literal: At that time Chief Minister Feng Dao composed a farewell poem; its striking lines read: "A Tang academician come from the north to draft edicts, a Han general going west bearing his commander's banner."
translations.idiomatic: Chief Minister Feng Dao wrote a farewell poem whose memorable lines ran: "A Tang academician come from the north to draft edicts, a Han general going west bearing his commander's banner."

sentences.zh: 儒者榮之。

translations.literal: Men of learning took it as an honor.
translations.idiomatic: Men of learning regarded this as a great honor.

sentences.zh: 明年，改賜耀忠匡定保節功臣，就加檢校司徒。

translations.literal: The next year he was granted the title of Meritorious Minister for Glorious Loyalty, Rectification, and Preservation of Integrity, and was further appointed acting Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was granted the title Meritorious Minister for Glorious Loyalty, Rectification, and Preservation of Integrity and was further promoted to acting Minister of Education.

sentences.zh: 三年，入拜兵部尚書，判太僕卿事。

translations.literal: In the third year he entered court and was appointed Minister of War, with concurrent duty as acting Director of the Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he entered court as Minister of War and was concurrently charged with the duties of Director of the Imperial Stud.

sentences.zh: 四年，進封開國公。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was advanced in enfeoffment to Duke Who Establishes the State.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was enfeoffed as Duke Who Establishes the State.

sentences.zh: 長興二年，授檢校太保、河陽節度使，未幾，移鎮滄州，入為右僕射。

translations.literal: In the second year of Changxing he was appointed acting Grand Mentor and military governor of Heyang; before long he was transferred to command Cang Prefecture, then entered court as Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Changxing he was appointed acting Grand Mentor and military governor of Heyang; soon he was transferred to Cang Prefecture, then recalled to court as Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 及秦王得罪，奉詔權知河南府事。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Qin fell from favor, he received an edict to act as temporary administrator of Henan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Qin fell from favor, he was ordered to serve as acting administrator of Henan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 應順初，遷檢校太傅，正拜河南尹，後改太子少師。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yingshun he was promoted to acting Grand Preceptor and formally appointed Governor of Henan; later he was changed to Junior Tutor to the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Yingshun he was promoted to acting Grand Preceptor and formally appointed Governor of Henan; he was later made Junior Tutor to the Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 清泰末，復為右僕射。

translations.literal: At the end of Qingtai he again became Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Qingtai he again became Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 高祖登極，質以微恙分司洛宅。

translations.literal: When Gaozu ascended the throne, Zhi, because of a minor ailment, served in a nominal post at his Luoyang residence.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu took the throne, Zhi, suffering a minor illness, held a nominal post at his Luoyang residence.

sentences.zh: 少帝嗣位，拜太子太保。

translations.literal: When the Lesser Emperor succeeded to the throne, Zhi was appointed Grand Tutor to the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: When the Lesser Emperor succeeded to the throne, Zhi was appointed Grand Tutor to the Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 天福七年秋，卒於洛陽，年七十六。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the seventh year of Tianfu he died in Luoyang at age seventy-six.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of the seventh year of Tianfu he died in Luoyang at the age of seventy-six.

sentences.zh: 累贈太子太師，謚曰文忠。

translations.literal: He was posthumously ennobled through successive promotions to Grand Preceptor to the Crown Prince, and was given the posthumous title Wenzhong.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously promoted by successive honors to Grand Preceptor to the Crown Prince and was given the posthumous title Wenzhong.

sentences.zh: 〈（《五代會要》：漢乾祐元年九月，其子尚書兵部員外郎盧瓊上章請謚，下太常議，謚曰文忠。）〉

translations.literal: (From the Essentials of the Five Dynasties: In the ninth month of the first year of Gan you of Han, his son Lu Qiong, Outer Director in the Bureau of Military Affairs under the Ministry of War, submitted a memorial requesting a posthumous title; the matter was referred to the Court of Imperial Sacrifices for deliberation, and the posthumous title Wenzhong was granted.)〉
translations.idiomatic: (From the Essentials of the Five Dynasties: In the ninth month of the first year of Gan you of Han, his son Lu Qiong, Outer Director in the Bureau of Military Affairs under the Ministry of War, submitted a memorial requesting a posthumous title; the Court of Imperial Sacrifices was ordered to deliberate, and the posthumous title Wenzhong was granted.)〉

sentences.zh: 子十一人，唯第六子夏，仕至省郎，余歷州縣焉。

translations.literal: He had eleven sons; only the sixth, Xia, rose to office as a director in a central ministry, while the rest served in prefectural and county posts.
translations.idiomatic: He had eleven sons; only the sixth, Xia, rose to a directorship in a central ministry, while the others served in prefectural and county posts.

sentences.zh: 李專美，字翊商，京兆萬年人也。

translations.literal: Li Zhuanmei, courtesy name Yishang, was a man of Wannian in Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zhuanmei, whose courtesy name was Yishang, came from Wannian in Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 曾祖隨，光祿卿。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Sui was Director of the Imperial Banquets.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Sui had been Director of the Imperial Banquets.

sentences.zh: 祖正範，尚書庫部郎中。

translations.literal: His grandfather Zhengfan was Director in the Bureau of Storehouses under the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Zhengfan had been Director in the Bureau of Storehouses under the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 專美少篤學文，以父樞唐昭宗時常應進士舉，為覆試所落，不許再入，專美心愧之，由是不遊文場。

translations.literal: Zhuanmei from youth was devoted to learning and literature; because his father Shu in the time of Emperor Zhaozong of Tang had once entered the presented-scholar examination and was failed in the repeat examination and not permitted to enter again, Zhuanmei felt ashamed in his heart and on this account did not enter the literary arena.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuanmei from youth was devoted to scholarship and letters. His father Shu had once taken the presented-scholar examination under Emperor Zhaozong of Tang but was failed in the repeat examination and barred from re-entry; ashamed on his father's account, Zhuanmei never entered the examination arena himself.

sentences.zh: 偽梁貞明中，河南尹張全義以專美名族之後，奏為陸渾尉，秩滿，改舞陽令。

translations.literal: In the Zhenming era of the false Liang, Zhang Quanyi, Governor of Henan, because Zhuanmei was descended from a famous clan, memorialized the throne to appoint him sheriff of Luhun; when his term expired he was changed to magistrate of Wuyang.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhenming era of the Liang, Zhang Quanyi, Governor of Henan, because Zhuanmei came from a distinguished clan, had him appointed sheriff of Luhun; when his term ended he was made magistrate of Wuyang.

sentences.zh: 專美性廉謹，大著政聲。

translations.literal: Zhuanmei's nature was incorrupt and cautious, and he won great renown for his governance.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuanmei was by nature incorrupt and cautious, and his administrative reputation was excellent.

sentences.zh: 後唐天成中，安邑榷鹽使李肅辟為推官，時唐末帝鎮河中，見其敦雅，心重之。

translations.literal: In the Tiancheng era of Later Tang, Li Su, commissioner for the salt monopoly at Anyi, recruited him as investigating officer; at that time the Last Emperor of Tang was military governor of Hezhong, saw his earnest refinement, and valued him in his heart.
translations.idiomatic: In the Tiancheng era of Later Tang, Li Su, commissioner for the salt monopoly at Anyi, recruited him as investigating officer. The Last Emperor of Tang was then military governor of Hezhong; seeing Zhuanmei's earnest refinement, he came to esteem him highly.

sentences.zh: 末帝一日曾召肅宴於衙署，專美亦預坐，末帝謂肅曰：「某夜來夢主上召去，與宋王同剃卻頭，何也？」

translations.literal: One day the Last Emperor summoned Su to a banquet at the government office; Zhuanmei also took a seat. The Last Emperor said to Su: "Last night I dreamed that the sovereign summoned me away and that the Prince of Song and I had our heads shaved together—what does this mean?"
translations.idiomatic: One day the Last Emperor summoned Su to a banquet at headquarters; Zhuanmei was also present. The Last Emperor said to Su: "Last night I dreamed that the sovereign summoned me and that the Prince of Song and I had our heads shaved together—what can this mean?"

sentences.zh: 坐客都無對者，專美屏人謂曰：「將來必為嗣主。」

translations.literal: None of the guests present had any reply; Zhuanmei, drawing him aside from others, said: "In the future you will certainly become the heir sovereign."
translations.idiomatic: None of the guests could answer. Zhuanmei drew him aside and said: "You will surely become the heir sovereign."

sentences.zh: 由是愈重焉。

translations.literal: From this he valued him all the more.
translations.idiomatic: From that time the Last Emperor valued him all the more.

sentences.zh: 末帝留守長安，奏為從事，及移鎮鳳翔，遷為記室。

translations.literal: When the Last Emperor was regent at Chang'an, he memorialized the throne to appoint Zhuanmei as staff officer; when he was transferred to command Fengxiang, Zhuanmei was promoted to recorder.
translations.idiomatic: When the Last Emperor served as regent at Chang'an, he had Zhuanmei appointed as staff officer; when he was transferred to Fengxiang, Zhuanmei was promoted to recorder.

sentences.zh: 末帝即位，除尚書庫部郎中，賜金紫，充樞密院直學士。

translations.literal: When the Last Emperor ascended the throne, Zhuanmei was appointed Director in the Bureau of Storehouses under the Ministry of Works, granted the gold seal and purple robe, and made direct academician of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When the Last Emperor took the throne, Zhuanmei was appointed Director in the Bureau of Storehouses, granted the gold seal and purple robe, and made direct academician of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 初，末帝起自鳳翔，大許諸軍厚賞。

translations.literal: At first, when the Last Emperor rose from Fengxiang, he had promised the armies lavish rewards.
translations.idiomatic: When the Last Emperor first rose from Fengxiang, he had promised the armies lavish rewards.

sentences.zh: 洎至洛陽，閱內庫金帛不過二三萬，尋又配率京城戶民，雖行捶楚，亦所獲無幾，末帝憂之。

translations.literal: When he reached Luoyang and examined the inner treasury, gold and silk amounted to no more than twenty or thirty thousand; soon he also levied assessments on the households of the capital, and even though beating was applied, what was obtained was very little, and the Last Emperor was troubled.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached Luoyang and inspected the inner treasury, he found no more than twenty or thirty thousand in gold and silk. He then levied assessments on the capital's households, but even with beatings the yield was meager, and the Last Emperor was deeply troubled.

sentences.zh: 會專美宿於禁中，末帝召而讓之曰：「卿士人子弟，常言有才術，今致我至此，不能度運以濟時事，留才術何施也！」

translations.literal: Once when Zhuanmei was lodging in the palace precincts, the Last Emperor summoned and reproached him, saying: "You are the son of a scholar-official family and always speak of having talent and skill; yet you have brought me to this pass and cannot gauge the times to rescue current affairs—of what use is talent and skill left behind!"
translations.idiomatic: Once when Zhuanmei was staying in the palace, the Last Emperor summoned and rebuked him: "You are the son of a scholar-official family and always claim talent and ability—yet you have brought me to this pass and cannot read the times to rescue the situation. What good is talent left unused?"

sentences.zh: 專美惶恐待罪，良久奏曰：「臣才力駑劣，屬當興運，陛下猥垂錄任，無以裨益聖朝，然府藏空竭，軍賞不給，非臣之罪也。

translations.literal: Zhuanmei, in fear and trembling awaiting punishment, after a long while submitted: "Your servant's talent and strength are mean and inferior; I happened to meet a time of rising fortune, and Your Majesty condescended to employ me, yet I have been unable to benefit the sagely court. Nevertheless, the treasury is empty and exhausted and army rewards cannot be supplied—this is not your servant's fault.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuanmei, trembling with fear, waited a long while and then replied: "Your servant's abilities are mean, and though I have had the honor of serving in a time of rising fortune, I have been unable to benefit the court. Yet the treasury is empty and army rewards cannot be paid—this is not my fault.

sentences.zh: 臣思明宗棄代之際，是時府庫濫賞已竭，繼以鄂王臨朝，紀綱大壞，縱有無限之財賦，不能滿驕軍溪壑之心，所以陛下孤立岐陽而得天下。

translations.literal: Your servant reflects that at the time when Mingzong passed from the throne, the treasury had already been drained by indiscriminate rewards; this was followed by the Prince of E's holding court, when statutes and discipline were greatly ruined; even if there had been limitless wealth and revenue, it could not have filled the insatiable hearts of the arrogant armies. That is why Your Majesty, isolated at Qiyang, was able to gain the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Consider Mingzong's death: the treasury had already been drained by reckless rewards. Then the Prince of E held court and discipline collapsed utterly. Even limitless wealth could not have satisfied the insatiable armies. That is why Your Majesty, standing alone at Qiyang, was able to win the realm.

sentences.zh: 臣以為國之存亡，不專在行賞，須刑政立於上，恥格行於下，賞當功，罰當罪，則近於理道也。

translations.literal: Your servant considers that whether a state survives or perishes does not depend solely on dispensing rewards; punishments and government must be established above, and the sense of shame must operate below; rewards must match merit and punishments must match crimes—then one approaches the way of reason.
translations.idiomatic: I believe a state's survival does not depend on rewards alone. Punishment and government must be established above, and the sense of shame must operate below; rewards must match merit and punishments must match crimes—then one approaches the way of good governance.

sentences.zh: 若陛下不改覆車之轍，以賞無賴之軍，徒困蒸民，存亡未可知也。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty does not change the track of the overturned cart and uses rewards to satisfy unruly armies, you will only weary the common people, and whether the state survives or perishes cannot be known.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty does not turn from the path that overturned the cart and keeps rewarding unruly troops, you will only exhaust the people, and whether the state survives is uncertain.

sentences.zh: 今宜取見在財賦以給之，不必踐前言而希茍悅。」

translations.literal: Now you should take the wealth and revenue presently available to supply them; you need not fulfill earlier words in hope of momentary favor."
translations.idiomatic: You should pay them from wealth and revenue actually on hand, and need not fulfill your earlier promises merely to win momentary favor."

sentences.zh: 末帝然之。

translations.literal: The Last Emperor approved of this.
translations.idiomatic: The Last Emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 及其行賞，雖不愜於軍士，然洛陽戶民獲免鞭笞之苦，由專美之敷揚也。

translations.literal: When rewards were distributed, although the soldiers were not satisfied, the households of Luoyang were spared the pain of the whip and cudgel—this was due to Zhuanmei's exposition and advocacy.
translations.idiomatic: When rewards were distributed the soldiers were dissatisfied, but the households of Luoyang were spared the lash—thanks to Zhuanmei's advocacy.

sentences.zh: 尋轉給事中，明年，遷兵部侍郎、端明殿學士，未幾，改檢校尚書右僕射、守秘書監，充宣徽北院使。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Supervising Censor; the next year he was promoted to Vice Minister of War and academician of the Hall of Brilliant Governance; before long he was changed to acting Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, acting Director of the Imperial Library, and Commissioner of the Northern Bureau of the Palace Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made Supervising Censor; the next year he was promoted to Vice Minister of War and academician of the Hall of Brilliant Governance; before long he was made acting Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, acting Director of the Imperial Library, and Commissioner of the Northern Bureau of the Palace Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 高祖入洛，以例除名。

translations.literal: When Gaozu entered Luoyang, Zhuanmei was removed from office according to precedent.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu entered Luoyang, Zhuanmei was removed from office according to precedent.

sentences.zh: 三年，復授衛尉少卿，繼遷鴻臚、大理卿。

translations.literal: In the third year he was again appointed Vice Director of the Imperial Ancestral Temple; he was subsequently promoted to Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments and Director of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was again appointed Vice Director of the Imperial Ancestral Temple and was subsequently promoted to Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments and Director of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 開運中，以病卒，時年六十二。

translations.literal: In the Kaiyun era he died of illness at age sixty-two.
translations.idiomatic: During the Kaiyun era he died of illness at the age of sixty-two.

sentences.zh: 專美之遠祖本出姑臧大房，與清河小房崔氏、北祖第二房盧氏、昭國鄭氏為四望族，皆不以才行相尚，不以軒冕為貴，雖布衣徒步，視公卿蔑如也。

translations.literal: Zhuanmei's remote ancestors originally came from the great branch of the clan at Guzang; together with the minor branch of the Cui clan of Qinghe, the second branch of the northern ancestor of the Lu clan, and the Zheng clan of Zhaoguo they formed the four eminent clans. None of them valued one another for conduct or talent, nor regarded carriage and cap as honorable; even in plain cloth and on foot they looked down on dukes and ministers as if they were nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuanmei's remote ancestors came from the great branch of the clan at Guzang. Together with the minor branch of the Cui of Qinghe, the second northern branch of the Lu, and the Zheng of Zhaoguo they formed the four eminent clans. None prized conduct or talent in one another, nor regarded rank and office as honorable; even in plain dress and on foot they looked down on dukes and ministers as beneath notice.

sentences.zh: 男女婚嫁，不雜他姓，欲聘其族，厚贈金帛始許焉。

translations.literal: In marriage for men and women they did not mix with other surnames; those who wished to betroth into their clans had first to present lavish gifts of gold and silk before consent was granted.
translations.idiomatic: In marriage they would not mix with other surnames; those who wished to marry into these clans had to offer lavish gifts of gold and silk before consent was granted.

sentences.zh: 唐太宗曾降詔以戒其弊風，終莫能改。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong of Tang once issued an edict to warn against this corrupt custom, yet in the end it could not be changed.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong of Tang once issued an edict warning against this corrupt custom, yet it could never be changed.

sentences.zh: 其間有未達者，必曰：「姓崔、盧、李、鄭了，余復何求耶！」

translations.literal: Among them those who had not yet attained office would invariably say: "One has the surnames Cui, Lu, Li, and Zheng—what more is there to seek!"
translations.idiomatic: Those among them who had not yet attained office would say: "One has the surnames Cui, Lu, Li, and Zheng—what more could one want!"

sentences.zh: 其遠者，則邈在天表，敻若千里，人罕造其門，浮薄自大，皆此類也。

translations.literal: The more remote among them were as distant as the heavens above, remote as a thousand li; people rarely came to their gates. Frivolous, shallow, and arrogant—all were of this kind.
translations.idiomatic: The more remote among them were as distant as the heavens, remote as a thousand li; people rarely crossed their thresholds. Frivolous, shallow, and arrogant—all were of this kind.

sentences.zh: 唯專美未嘗以氏族形於口吻，見寒素士大夫，恒恂恂如也，人以此多之。

translations.literal: Only Zhuanmei never let his clan name appear on his lips; when he met poor and plain scholar-officials he was always respectful and deferential, and people for this reason praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Only Zhuanmei never flaunted his clan name; toward poor and plain scholar-officials he was always respectful and deferential, and people praised him for it.

sentences.zh: 專美職岐下，曾夢具裳簡立嵩山之頂。

translations.literal: While Zhuanmei was serving below Qi, he once dreamed that he stood atop Mount Song fully robed and holding bamboo slips.
translations.idiomatic: While serving below Qi, Zhuanmei once dreamed that he stood atop Mount Song in full court dress holding bamboo slips.

sentences.zh: 及為端明殿學士，學士李崧同列而班在其上，因以所夢告崧，且言：「某非德非勛，安可久居此位，處吾子之首乎！」

translations.literal: When he became academician of the Hall of Brilliant Governance, Academician Li Song was of the same rank but stood above him in court order; he therefore told Song of his dream and moreover said: "I lack both virtue and merit—how can I long hold this position and stand above you!"
translations.idiomatic: When he became academician of the Hall of Brilliant Governance, Academician Li Song was his colleague but ranked above him in court order. He told Song of his dream and said: "I lack both virtue and merit—how can I long hold this position above you!"

sentences.zh: 因懇求他官，尋移宣徽使，崧深德之。

translations.literal: He therefore earnestly requested another office; soon he was transferred to Commissioner of the Palace Secretariat, and Song was deeply grateful to him.
translations.idiomatic: He earnestly requested another post and was soon transferred to Commissioner of the Palace Secretariat; Song was deeply grateful.

sentences.zh: 及高祖臨朝，崧為樞密使，與桑維翰同列，維翰與專美亦有舊，乃協力以奏之，遂復朝序，位至九卿。

translations.literal: When Gaozu held court, Song was Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs and sat in the same rank as Sang Weihan; Weihan also had old ties with Zhuanmei, and they therefore joined forces to memorialize on his behalf, whereupon he was restored to court order and rose to one of the nine ministers.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu held court, Song was Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs and sat with Sang Weihan; Weihan also had old ties with Zhuanmei, and together they memorialized on his behalf. He was restored to court rank and rose to one of the nine ministers.

sentences.zh: 專美曾使閩中，遇風水漂至兩浙，逾歲無恙而還，至是善終，人以為神道福謙之所致也。

translations.literal: Zhuanmei had once been sent on mission to Min; he encountered wind and waves and was carried adrift to the two Zhe regions, but after more than a year returned unharmed; when he now died a peaceful death, people considered it the result of the spirits' blessing the modest.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuanmei had once been sent on mission to Min; he was driven by storm to the two Zhe regions but returned unharmed after more than a year. When he now died a peaceful death, people attributed it to the spirits rewarding his modesty.

sentences.zh: 盧詹，字楚良，京兆長安人也。

translations.literal: Lu Zhan, courtesy name Chuliang, was a man of Chang'an in Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Zhan, whose courtesy name was Chuliang, came from Chang'an in Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 唐天祐中，爲河中從事。

translations.literal: During the Tianyou era of Tang he served as staff officer in Hezhong.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianyou era of Tang he served as staff officer in Hezhong.

sentences.zh: 莊宗即位，擢爲員外郎、知制誥，遷中書舍人。

translations.literal: When Zhuangzong took the throne, he was promoted to outer director and controller of edicts, then transferred to secretariat drafter.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhuangzong took the throne, he was promoted to outer director and controller of edicts, then transferred to secretariat drafter.

sentences.zh: 天成中，拜禮部侍郎、知貢舉，歷御史中丞、兵部侍郎、尚書左丞、工部尚書。

translations.literal: During Tiancheng he was appointed vice minister of rites and supervisor of tribute examinations, and successively served as censor-in-chief, vice minister of war, left assistant director of the Department of State Affairs, and minister of works.
translations.idiomatic: During Tiancheng he was appointed vice minister of rites and supervisor of tribute examinations, and successively served as censor-in-chief, vice minister of war, left assistant director of the Department of State Affairs, and minister of works.

sentences.zh: 詹性剛直，議論不避權貴，執政者常惡之。

translations.literal: Zhan was by nature forthright and upright; in debate he did not spare powerful nobles, and those in power often hated him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhan was by nature forthright and upright; in debate he did not spare powerful nobles, and those in power often hated him.

sentences.zh: 天福初，拜禮部尚書，分司洛下，與右僕射盧質、散騎常侍盧重俱在西都，數相過從。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianfu he was appointed minister of rites and held a nominal post at Luoyang. Together with Right Vice Director Lu Zhi and Regular Attendant Lu Chong, he was all in the western capital, and they frequently visited one another.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Tianfu he was appointed minister of rites and held a nominal post at Luoyang. Together with Right Vice Director Lu Zhi and Regular Attendant Lu Chong, he was in the western capital, and they frequently visited one another.

sentences.zh: 三人俱嗜酒，好遊山水，塔廟林亭花竹之地，無不同往，酣飲爲樂，人無間然，洛中朝士目爲「三盧會」。

translations.literal: All three loved wine and enjoyed touring mountains and rivers; to pagodas, temples, wooded pavilions, and places of flowers and bamboo they went together without exception. They made merry drinking to their hearts' content, and no one found fault with them; the court gentlemen of Luoyang called them the "Three Lu Assembly."
translations.idiomatic: All three loved wine and enjoyed touring mountains and rivers. To pagodas, temples, wooded pavilions, and places of flowers and bamboo they went together without exception, drinking merrily for pleasure, and no one found fault with them. The court gentlemen of Luoyang called them the "Three Lu Assembly."

sentences.zh: 常委順性命，不營財利。

translations.literal: He always submitted to fate and did not pursue wealth.
translations.idiomatic: He always submitted to fate and did not pursue wealth.

sentences.zh: 開運初，卒於洛陽。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaiyun he died in Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Kaiyun he died in Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 詹家無長物，喪具不給，少帝聞之，賜布帛百段，粟麥百斛，方能襄其葬事。

translations.literal: Zhan's household had few possessions and could not supply funeral goods. When the Lesser Emperor heard of this, he granted a hundred bolts of cloth and silk and a hundred hu of grain and wheat, only then enabling his burial to be properly carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Zhan's household had few possessions and could not supply funeral goods. When the Lesser Emperor heard of this, he granted a hundred bolts of cloth and silk and a hundred hu of grain and wheat, enabling his burial to be properly carried out.

sentences.zh: 贈太子少保。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted the title Junior Tutor to the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted the title Junior Tutor to the Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 崔棁，字子文，博陵安平人。

translations.literal: Cui Zhuo, courtesy name Ziwen, was a man of Anping in Boling.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Zhuo, whose courtesy name was Ziwen, came from Anping in Boling.

sentences.zh: 累世冠冕。

translations.literal: For generations his family had worn caps and held office.
translations.idiomatic: For generations his family had held high office.

sentences.zh: 曾祖元受，舉進士，直史館。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Yuanshou passed the presented-scholar examination and served in the Historiography Institute.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Yuanshou had passed the presented-scholar examination and served in the Historiography Institute.

sentences.zh: 祖銖，安、濮二州刺史。

translations.literal: His grandfather Zhuo was prefect of An and Pu prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Zhuo had been prefect of An and Pu prefectures.

sentences.zh: 父涿，刑部郎中。

translations.literal: His father Zhuo was Director in the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zhuo had been Director in the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 棁少好學，梁貞明三年，舉進士甲科，為開封尹王瓚從事。

translations.literal: Zhuo from youth loved learning; in the third year of Zhenming of Liang he passed the presented-scholar examination in the first class and became staff officer to Wang Zan, Governor of Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Zhuo loved learning. In the third year of Zhenming of Liang he passed the presented-scholar examination in the first class and became staff officer to Wang Zan, Governor of Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 棁性至孝，父涿有疾，謂親友曰：「死生有命，無醫為也。」

translations.literal: Zhuo's nature was supremely filial; when his father Zhuo fell ill, he told relatives and friends: "Life and death have their mandate; there is no use in physicians."
translations.idiomatic: Zhuo was supremely filial. When his father Zhuo fell ill, the father told relatives and friends: "Life and death are fated; physicians are of no use."

sentences.zh: 棁侍之衣不解帶，有賓至，必拜泣告於門外，請方便勸其進藥，涿終莫之從。

translations.literal: Zhuo attended him without undoing his belt; when guests came he would always bow and weep and report at the outer gate, asking them to find an opportune moment to urge his father to take medicine, but Zhuo the father never followed this.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuo attended him without removing his belt even to sleep. When guests came he would bow and weep at the gate and ask them to urge his father to take medicine, but the father never consented.

sentences.zh: 及丁憂，哀毀過制。

translations.literal: When he entered mourning his grief and devastation exceeded the prescribed norms.
translations.idiomatic: In mourning his grief exceeded the prescribed norms.

sentences.zh: 明宗朝，授監察御史，不應命，逾年詔再下，乃就列焉。

translations.literal: In the reign of Mingzong he was appointed Investigating Censor but did not accept the commission; after more than a year the edict was issued again, and only then did he take his place in the ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Under Mingzong he was appointed Investigating Censor but declined; after more than a year the edict was issued again, and only then did he take up the post.

sentences.zh: 累遷都官郎中、翰林學士。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to Director in the Bureau of Justice and Academician of the Hanlin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted in succession to Director in the Bureau of Justice and Academician of the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 天福初，以戶部侍郎為學士承旨。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianfu he served as Vice Minister of Revenue and Chief Academician.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Tianfu he served as Vice Minister of Revenue and Chief Academician.

sentences.zh: 嘗草制，為宰相桑維翰所改，棁以唐故事，學士草制有所改者，當罷職，乃引經據爭，維翰不能詰，命權知二年貢舉。

translations.literal: Once when he drafted an edict it was altered by Chief Minister Sang Weihan; Zhuo cited Tang precedent that when an academician's draft edict was altered he should be removed from office, and therefore cited classics and argued on principle; Weihan could not refute him and ordered him to act temporarily as supervisor of the second year's tribute examinations.
translations.idiomatic: Once when he drafted an edict Chief Minister Sang Weihan altered it. Zhuo cited Tang precedent that when an academician's draft was altered the academician should be removed from office, and argued from classical authority; Weihan could not refute him and appointed him acting supervisor of the second year's tribute examinations.

sentences.zh: 時有進士孔英者，素有醜行，為當時所惡，棁受命往見維翰，維翰語素簡，謂棁曰：「孔英來矣。」

translations.literal: At that time there was a presented scholar named Kong Ying who had long had disgraceful conduct and was detested by his contemporaries; Zhuo received his commission and went to see Weihan; Weihan's words were always brief, and he said to Zhuo: "Kong Ying has come."
translations.idiomatic: At that time there was a presented scholar named Kong Ying notorious for disgraceful conduct and detested by all. When Zhuo received his commission and went to see Weihan, Weihan spoke briefly and said to Zhuo: "Kong Ying has come."

sentences.zh: 棁不諭其意，以謂維翰以孔英為言，乃考英及第，物議大以為非，遂罷學士，拜尚書左丞，遷太常卿。

translations.literal: Zhuo did not understand his meaning and supposed that Weihan was speaking of Kong Ying; he therefore passed Ying in the examination and ranked him among those who received degrees. Public opinion greatly condemned this as wrong, and he was therefore removed as academician, appointed Left Assistant Director of the Department of State Affairs, and promoted to Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuo misunderstood and thought Weihan meant to pass Kong Ying; he therefore passed Ying and ranked him among the degree recipients. Public opinion condemned this roundly, and Zhuo was removed as academician, appointed Left Assistant Director of the Department of State Affairs, and promoted to Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 後以風痹改太子賓客，分司西京。

translations.literal: Later, because of wind paralysis he was changed to Tutor to the Crown Prince and served in a nominal post at the western capital.
translations.idiomatic: Later, afflicted with wind paralysis, he was made Tutor to the Crown Prince and held a nominal post at the western capital.

sentences.zh: 卒年六十八。

translations.literal: He died at age sixty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of sixty-eight.

sentences.zh: 棁平生所著文章、碑誄、制詔甚多，人有借本傳寫者，則曰：「有前賢，有來者，奚用此為！」

translations.literal: Throughout his life Zhuo composed many essays, inscriptions, eulogies, and edicts; when people asked to borrow copies to transcribe them, he would say: "There were worthies before and there will be those who come after—what use is this!"
translations.idiomatic: Throughout his life Zhuo wrote many essays, inscriptions, eulogies, and edicts. When people asked to borrow copies to transcribe, he would say: "There were worthies before and there will be those who come after—what use is this!"

sentences.zh: 凡受托而作者，必親劄致之，即焚其槁，懼泄人之假手也。

translations.literal: For every piece he undertook by commission he would personally deliver it in a letter and immediately burn the draft, fearing that others might leak it through borrowed hands.
translations.idiomatic: For every commissioned piece he would deliver it personally in a letter and immediately burn the draft, fearing that others might circulate it through borrowed hands.

sentences.zh: 棁笑不至矧，怒不至詈，接新進後生，未嘗無誨焉。

translations.literal: When Zhuo laughed it did not reach a grin; when he was angry it did not reach cursing; when he received newly advanced younger men he never failed to offer instruction.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhuo laughed it never reached a broad grin; when angry he never reached cursing; toward newly advanced younger men he always offered instruction.

sentences.zh: 群居公會端坐寡言，嘗雲非止致人愛憎，且或幹人祖禰之諱。

translations.literal: In group gatherings at public assemblies he sat upright and spoke little, once saying that this was not only to avoid arousing love or hatred in others, but also lest one touch upon the taboo names of people's ancestors.
translations.idiomatic: At public gatherings he sat upright and spoke little, saying that this was not only to avoid arousing love or hatred but also lest one touch upon people's ancestral taboo names.

sentences.zh: 指命仆役，亦用禮節，盛暑祁寒，不使冒犯。

translations.literal: When he directed and commanded servants he also used ritual propriety; in blazing summer heat or bitter winter cold he did not allow them to be offended or harmed.
translations.idiomatic: Even when directing servants he observed ritual propriety; in blazing summer or bitter winter he would not let them suffer offense or harm.

sentences.zh: 嘗自話於知友云：「某少時，夢二人前引行路，一人計地裏，曰：『一舍矣，可以止。』

translations.literal: He once told a close friend: "In my youth I dreamed that two men walked ahead leading me on the road; one counted the distance in li and said: 'One stage has been reached; you may stop.'
translations.idiomatic: He once told a close friend: "In my youth I dreamed that two men walked ahead leading me on the road; one counted the distance in li and said: 'One stage has been reached; you may stop.'

sentences.zh: 一人曰：『此君當更進三十有八里。』

translations.literal: The other said: 'This gentleman should go thirty-eight li farther.'
translations.idiomatic: The other said: 'This gentleman should go thirty-eight li farther.'

sentences.zh: 復行如所言，二人皆止之，俄而驚覺。」

translations.literal: They went on as he had said; both men stopped him, and presently he awoke with a start."
translations.idiomatic: They went on as he had said; both men stopped him, and presently he awoke with a start."

sentences.zh: 棁常識是夢，以為定命之限，故六十七請退，明年果終焉。

translations.literal: Zhuo often recognized that it was a dream and regarded it as the limit ordained by fate; therefore at the age of sixty-seven he asked to retire, and the following year he indeed met his end.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuo often knew it for a dream and took it as the limit ordained by fate; at sixty-seven he asked to retire, and the next year he died as foretold.

sentences.zh: 兄棆，有隱德，好釋氏，閑居滑州。

translations.literal: His elder brother Lun possessed hidden virtue, loved Buddhism, and lived in retirement at Hua Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Lun was a man of quiet virtue who loved Buddhism and lived in retirement at Hua Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 嘗欲訪人於白馬津北，及臨岸，嘆曰：「波勢洶湧如此，安可濟乎！」

translations.literal: Once he wished to visit someone north of the Baima Ferry; when he came to the bank, he sighed and said: "The waves surge so fiercely—how could one cross!"
translations.idiomatic: Once he wished to visit someone north of the Baima Ferry, but when he reached the bank he sighed and said, "The waves surge so fiercely—how could anyone cross?"

sentences.zh: 乃止。

translations.literal: So he stopped.
translations.idiomatic: So he gave up and turned back.

sentences.zh: 後征拜左拾遺，辭疾不赴。

translations.literal: Later he was summoned and appointed Left Reminder; he pleaded illness and did not take up the post.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was summoned and appointed Left Reminder, but he pleaded illness and declined the appointment.

sentences.zh: 薛融，汾州平遙人。

translations.literal: Xue Rong was a man of Pingyao in Fen Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Rong came from Pingyao in Fen Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 性純和，以儒學為業。

translations.literal: His nature was pure and gentle; he made Confucian learning his profession.
translations.idiomatic: His nature was pure and gentle, and he devoted himself to Confucian learning.

sentences.zh: 初從雲州帥李存璋為幕職，唐莊宗平河南，歷鄆、徐二鎮從事。

translations.literal: At first he followed the military governor of Yun Prefecture, Li Cunzhang, as a staff member; when Zhuangzong of Tang pacified Henan, he successively served as aide in the two prefectures of Yan and Xu.
translations.idiomatic: He first served on the staff of Li Cunzhang, military governor of Yun Prefecture; after Zhuangzong of Tang pacified Henan, he held aide posts in Yan and Xu in succession.

sentences.zh: 明宗初，授華州節度判官。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Mingzong's reign, he was appointed military governor's aide at Hua Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Mingzong's reign he was appointed military governor's aide at Hua Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 長興四年，入為右補闕，直宏文館，歲餘，改河東觀察判官，會高祖鎮太原，遂居於幕府。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Changxing he entered court as Right Supplements Censor and served in the Hongwen Pavilion; after more than a year he was transferred to be aide to the Hedong observation commissioner. When Gaozu was stationed at Taiyuan, he thus took up residence in the military governor's staff.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Changxing he entered court as Right Supplements Censor and served in the Hongwen Pavilion. After a little over a year he was transferred to be aide to the Hedong observation commissioner, and when Gaozu was stationed at Taiyuan he joined the governor's staff.

sentences.zh: 清泰末，高祖將舉義，延賓席而歷問之，次及融，對曰：「融本儒生，只曾讀三五卷書，至於軍旅之事，進退存亡之機，未之學也。」

translations.literal: At the end of Qingtai, when Gaozu was about to raise the banner of rebellion, he extended the guest seats and questioned each man in turn; when it came to Rong, he replied: "Rong is originally a Confucian scholar and has read only three or five volumes of books; as for military affairs and the timing of advance, retreat, survival, and destruction, I have not studied them."
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of Qingtai, as Gaozu prepared to raise the banner of rebellion, he gathered his guests and questioned each in turn. When it came to Rong, he answered, "I am only a Confucian scholar who has read a few volumes of books. As for military affairs and the timing of advance, retreat, survival, and destruction, I have never studied them."

sentences.zh: 座中聳然。

translations.literal: The assembly was stirred to attention.
translations.idiomatic: The whole assembly sat up in astonishment.

sentences.zh: 及登極，遷尚書吏部郎中兼侍御史知雜事。

translations.literal: When Gaozu ascended the throne, Rong was promoted to Director in the Ministry of Personnel of the Department of State Affairs, concurrently serving as Attendant Censor with charge of miscellaneous matters.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu took the throne, Rong was promoted to Director in the Ministry of Personnel and concurrently appointed Attendant Censor with charge of miscellaneous censorial duties.

sentences.zh: 天福二年，自左諫議大夫遷中書舍人，自以文學非優，不敢拜命，復為諫議。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianfu he was transferred from Left Remonstrance Grand Master to Drafting Secretary; deeming himself not superior in literary skill, he did not dare accept the appointment and returned to the post of remonstrance official.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Tianfu he was transferred from Left Remonstrance Grand Master to Drafting Secretary, but believing himself not strong enough in literary skill, he did not dare accept the appointment and returned to his former remonstrance post.

sentences.zh: 時詔修西京大內，融以鄴下用兵，國用不足，上疏復罷之，

translations.literal: At the time an edict ordered the repair of the inner palace at the Western Capital; Rong, noting that troops were engaged below Ye and state funds were insufficient, submitted a memorial requesting that the project again be cancelled,
translations.idiomatic: At the time an edict ordered repairs to the inner palace at the Western Capital. Rong submitted a memorial arguing that with troops engaged below Ye and state funds exhausted, the project should again be cancelled,

sentences.zh: 〈（《通鑒》：薛融諫曰：「今宮室雖經焚毀，猶侈於帝堯之茅茨；

translations.literal: (Zizhi Tongjian: Xue Rong remonstrated, saying: "Although the palace halls have been burned, they are still more lavish than Emperor Yao's thatched huts;
translations.idiomatic: (Zizhi Tongjian: Xue Rong remonstrated, saying, "Although the palace halls have been burned, they are still more lavish than Emperor Yao's thatched huts;

sentences.zh: 所費雖寡，猶多於漢文之露臺。

translations.literal: Although the expense is small, it is still greater than Emperor Wen of Han's open terrace.
translations.idiomatic: and although the expense may be small, it is still greater than Emperor Wen of Han's open terrace.

sentences.zh: 況魏城未下，公私困窘，誠非陛下修宮館之日。

translations.literal: Moreover, the city of Wei has not yet fallen and both public and private resources are strained—this is truly not the day for Your Majesty to repair palace halls.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the city of Wei has not yet fallen and both public and private resources are strained. This is truly not the time for Your Majesty to repair palace halls.

sentences.zh: 俟海內平寧，修之未晚。」）〉

translations.literal: When the realm within the seas is pacified and tranquil, it will not be too late to repair them."）〉
translations.idiomatic: When the realm is pacified and tranquil, it will not be too late to repair them."）〉

sentences.zh: 優詔嘉許。

translations.literal: An edict of praise commended him.
translations.idiomatic: An edict of warm praise commended him.

sentences.zh: 俄轉御史中丞，秩滿改尚書右丞，分司西都。

translations.literal: Shortly he was transferred to Censor-in-Chief; when his term expired he was changed to Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, serving at the Western Capital branch.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward he was transferred to Censor-in-Chief, and when his term expired he was appointed Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs at the Western Capital branch office.

sentences.zh: 天福六年，以疾卒，年六十餘。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Tianfu he died of illness, aged over sixty.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Tianfu he died of illness at over sixty years of age.

sentences.zh: 曹國珍，字彥輔，幽州固安人也。

translations.literal: Cao Guozhen, courtesy name Yanfu, was a man of Gu'an in You Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Guozhen, whose courtesy name was Yanfu, came from Gu'an in You Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 曾祖藹，祖蟾，父絢，代襲儒素。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather was Ai, his grandfather Chan, and his father Xuan; generation after generation they inherited the tradition of plain Confucian scholar-officials.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather was Ai, his grandfather Chan, and his father Xuan; for generations the family had upheld the tradition of plain Confucian scholar-officials.

sentences.zh: 國珍少值燕薊亂離，因落發被緇，客於河西延州，高萬興兄弟皆好文，辟為從事。

translations.literal: Guozhen in his youth encountered the chaos and displacement of Yan and Ji; he therefore tonsured himself and wore the black robe of a monk, living as a guest at Yan Prefecture west of the River. The brothers Gao Wanxing all loved literature and recruited him as an aide.
translations.idiomatic: In his youth Guozhen lived through the chaos and displacement of Yan and Ji. He tonsured himself and wore the black robe of a monk, then lived as a guest at Yan Prefecture west of the River, where the brothers Gao Wanxing, all lovers of literature, recruited him as an aide.

sentences.zh: 國珍常以文章自許，求貢禮闈，且掌書奏，期年，入為左拾遺，累遷至尚書郎。

translations.literal: Guozhen often prided himself on his literary compositions; he sought advancement through the metropolitan examination and also managed memorial drafts. Within a year he entered court as Left Reminder and was promoted in succession to become a Director in the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Guozhen often prided himself on his writing. He sought advancement through the metropolitan examination while also managing memorial drafts, and within a year he entered court as Left Reminder, rising in succession to become a Director in the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 每與人交，傾財無吝。

translations.literal: Whenever he associated with others, he spent his wealth freely without stint.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he associated with others, he spent his wealth freely and without stint.

sentences.zh: 性頗剛僻，經藝史學，非其所長，好自矜衒，多上章疏，文字差誤，數數有之，為縉紳所誚。

translations.literal: His nature was rather obstinate and aloof. Classical studies and historical learning were not his strengths, yet he loved to show himself off. He submitted many memorials and petitions, and textual errors in them occurred repeatedly, for which the gentry mocked him.
translations.idiomatic: His nature was obstinate and aloof. Classical studies and historical learning were not his strengths, yet he loved to show himself off. He submitted many memorials, and textual errors in them occurred again and again, for which the gentry mocked him.

sentences.zh: 高祖在藩時，嘗通私謁，以兄事之。

translations.literal: When Gaozu was still a prince, Guozhen had once visited him privately and treated him as an elder brother.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu was still a prince, Guozhen had once paid him a private visit and treated him as an elder brother.

sentences.zh: 及即位，國珍自比於嚴陵，上表敘舊，由是自吏部郎中拜左諫議大夫、給事中。

translations.literal: When Gaozu took the throne, Guozhen compared himself to Yan Ling and submitted a memorial recounting their old connection; he was therefore promoted from Director in the Ministry of Personnel to Left Remonstrance Grand Master and Chief Drafting Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu took the throne, Guozhen compared himself to Yan Ling and submitted a memorial recounting their old connection. He was therefore promoted from Director in the Ministry of Personnel to Left Remonstrance Grand Master and Chief Drafting Secretary.

sentences.zh: 〈（《歐陽史·張彥澤傳》：國珍與御史中丞王易簡率三院御史詣閣門，連疏論張彥澤，不報。）〉

translations.literal: (Ouyang Shi, Biography of Zhang Yanze: Guozhen and Censor-in-Chief Wang Yijian led the censors of the three bureaus to the Gate of Imperial Audience and submitted successive memorials denouncing Zhang Yanze, but received no response.)〉
translations.idiomatic: (Ouyang Shi, Biography of Zhang Yanze: Guozhen and Censor-in-Chief Wang Yijian led the censors of the three bureaus to the Gate of Imperial Audience and submitted successive memorials denouncing Zhang Yanze, but received no response.)〉

sentences.zh: 又求為御史中丞，時宰政不復為請，國珍銜之。

translations.literal: He also requested appointment as Censor-in-Chief, but the chief ministers did not again petition on his behalf; Guozhen resented this.
translations.idiomatic: He also requested appointment as Censor-in-Chief, but the chief ministers did not petition on his behalf again, and Guozhen resented it.

sentences.zh: 李崧之母薨，遣諸弟護喪歸葬深州，崧既起復，乃出北郊路隅設奠，公卿大夫皆送喪而出，國珍固爭不行，眾鹹推其讜直。

translations.literal: When Li Song's mother died, he sent his younger brothers to escort the funeral home for burial in Shen Prefecture. Since Song had already returned to office after mourning, he set out offerings at a roadside outside the northern suburbs. High ministers and officials all went out to send off the funeral procession, but Guozhen firmly objected and would not go; everyone praised his forthright integrity.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Song's mother died, he sent his younger brothers to escort the body home for burial in Shen Prefecture. Song had already returned to office after mourning and set out offerings at a roadside outside the northern suburbs. High ministers and officials all went out to send off the funeral procession, but Guozhen firmly objected and refused to go, and everyone praised his forthright integrity.

sentences.zh: 高祖晏駕，朝廷以宰臣馮道為山陵使，及靈盾既發，國珍上疏言：「馮道既為山陵使，不得復入都城，請除外佐，以桑維翰入輔。

translations.literal: When Gaozu passed away, the court appointed Chief Minister Feng Dao as commissioner for the imperial tomb. After the spirit shield had been dispatched, Guozhen submitted a memorial stating: "Since Feng Dao has been made commissioner for the imperial tomb, he should not again enter the capital; I request that auxiliary officials outside the capital be appointed, and that Sang Weihan enter to assist in governance.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu passed away, the court appointed Chief Minister Feng Dao commissioner for the imperial tomb. After the spirit shield had been dispatched, Guozhen submitted a memorial stating, "Since Feng Dao has been made commissioner for the imperial tomb, he should not again enter the capital. I request that outside auxiliary officials be appointed and that Sang Weihan enter to assist in governance.

sentences.zh: 李崧請罷相位，俾持喪制。」

translations.literal: Li Song should be asked to relinquish his chancellorship so that he may observe mourning."
translations.idiomatic: Li Song should be asked to relinquish his chancellorship so that he may observe mourning."

sentences.zh: 少帝覽奏，以所言侵越，出為陜州行軍司馬。

translations.literal: The Lesser Emperor reviewed the memorial and, deeming his words presumptuous and overstepping, dispatched him to serve as military adjutant at Shaan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The Lesser Emperor reviewed the memorial and, deeming his words presumptuous and overstepping, dispatched him to serve as military adjutant at Shaan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 至任悒怏，遘疾而卒。

translations.literal: Upon reaching his post he was discontent; he fell ill and died.
translations.idiomatic: Upon reaching his post he was discontent; he fell ill and died.

sentences.zh: 張仁願，字善政，開封陳留人也。

translations.literal: Zhang Renyuan, courtesy name Shanzheng, was a man of Chenliu in Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Renyuan, whose courtesy name was Shanzheng, came from Chenliu in Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 祖晸，唐右武衛大將軍。

translations.literal: His grandfather Zhao was Right Majordomo-General of the Martial Guard of Tang.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Zhao served as Right Majordomo-General of the Martial Guard under Tang.

sentences.zh: 父存敬，梁河中節度觀察留後，累贈中書令，《梁書》有傳。

translations.literal: His father Cunjing was military governor and observation commissioner of Hezhong under Liang, later posthumously ennobled through successive promotions to Central Secretariat Director; the Liang History contains his biography.
translations.idiomatic: His father Cunjing was military governor and observation commissioner of Hezhong under Liang and was posthumously ennobled through successive promotions to Central Secretariat Director; the Liang History contains his biography.

sentences.zh: 仁願梁貞明初，以勛臣之子起家為衛尉寺主簿，改著作佐郎、左贊善大夫，賜緋魚袋。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhenming under Liang, Renyuan as the son of a meritorious official began his career as secretary in the Court of Imperial Sacrifices; he was changed to Assistant Editor and Left Advisor to the Heir Apparent, and was granted the scarlet robe and fish tally.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Zhenming under Liang, Renyuan began his career as the son of a meritorious official, entering service as secretary in the Court of Imperial Sacrifices. He was then appointed Assistant Editor and Left Advisor to the Heir Apparent and granted the scarlet robe and fish tally.

sentences.zh: 唐同光初，遷大理正。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tongguang under Tang, he was transferred to Senior Judge in the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Tongguang under Tang, he was transferred to Senior Judge in the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 天成元年，自將作少監轉大理少卿。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tiancheng he was transferred from Vice Director of Palace Construction to Vice Director of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tiancheng he was transferred from Vice Director of Palace Construction to Vice Director of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 長興中，歷昭武、歸德兩鎮節度判官。

translations.literal: During Changxing he successively served as military governor's aide at the two prefectures of Zhaowu and Guide.
translations.idiomatic: During Changxing he served in succession as military governor's aide at Zhaowu and Guide.

sentences.zh: 四年，復入為大理少卿。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he again entered court as Vice Director of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he again entered court as Vice Director of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 清泰中，除殿中監。

translations.literal: During Qingtai he was appointed Supervisor of the Palace Receptions.
translations.idiomatic: During Qingtai he was appointed Supervisor of the Palace Receptions.

sentences.zh: 天福五年，拜大理卿。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Tianfu he was appointed Director of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Tianfu he was appointed Director of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 八年，轉光祿卿。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was transferred to Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he was transferred to Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 仁願性溫雅，明法書，累居詳刑之地，議讞疑獄，號為稱職。

translations.literal: Renyuan's nature was mild and refined; he was adept at legal writing. Having repeatedly held posts in judicial review, when he deliberated on doubtful cases he was acclaimed as fulfilling his duties.
translations.idiomatic: Renyuan was mild and refined by nature and skilled in legal writing. Having repeatedly held posts in judicial review, he was acclaimed as fulfilling his duties when he deliberated on doubtful cases.

sentences.zh: 兄仁穎，梁朝仕至諸衛將軍，中年以風恙廢於家凡十餘年，仁願事之，出告反面，如嚴父焉，士大夫推為孝友。

translations.literal: His elder brother Renying had served under Liang to the rank of general of the guard regiments; in midlife he was disabled at home by wind ailment for more than ten years. Renyuan attended him, asking permission on going out and returning to pay respects upon coming back, as to a strict father; scholar-officials praised his filial brotherly devotion.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Renying had served under Liang to the rank of general of the guard regiments, but in midlife he was disabled at home by wind ailment for more than ten years. Renyuan attended him, asking permission before going out and paying his respects upon returning, as to a strict father, and scholar-officials praised his filial brotherly devotion.

sentences.zh: 仁穎善理家，勤而且約，婦女衣不曳地，什物多歷年所，如新市焉。

translations.literal: Renying was skilled at managing the household—diligent and frugal; women's garments did not trail on the ground, and household goods even after many years were as if newly purchased.
translations.idiomatic: Renying was skilled at managing the household, diligent and frugal. Women's garments did not trail on the ground, and household goods even after many years looked as if newly purchased.

sentences.zh: 仁願開運元年再為大理卿，時隰州刺史王澈犯贓，朝廷以澈功臣之後，欲宥之，仁願累執奏不移，竟遣伏法，議者賞之。

translations.literal: In the first year of Kaiyun Renyuan again served as Director of Judicial Review. At the time Wang Che, prefect of Xi, was guilty of embezzlement; the court, considering Che a descendant of a meritorious minister, wished to pardon him, but Renyuan repeatedly submitted memorials without yielding, and Che was finally sent to execution; commentators praised him.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Kaiyun Renyuan again served as Director of Judicial Review. At the time Wang Che, prefect of Xi, was guilty of embezzlement, and the court, considering him a descendant of a meritorious minister, wished to pardon him. Renyuan repeatedly submitted memorials without yielding, and Che was finally executed; commentators praised him.

sentences.zh: 開運二年，以疾卒，年五十一。

translations.literal: In the second year of Kaiyun he died of illness at fifty-one.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Kaiyun he died of illness at fifty-one.

sentences.zh: 贈秘書監。

translations.literal: Posthumously granted Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously granted Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 趙熙，字績巨，唐宰相齊國公光逢之猶子也。

translations.literal: Zhao Xi, courtesy name Jiju, was the nephew by marriage of Tang chancellor Duke of Qi, Guangfeng.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Xi, whose courtesy name was Jiju, was the nephew of Tang chancellor Zhao Guangfeng, Duke of Qi.

sentences.zh: 起家授秘書省校書郎，唐天成中，累遷至起居郎。

translations.literal: He began his career appointed as proofreader in the Secretariat; during Tiancheng under Tang he was promoted in succession to Diarist.
translations.idiomatic: He began his career as proofreader in the Secretariat, and during Tiancheng under Tang he rose in succession to Diarist.

sentences.zh: 數上章言事，以稱旨尋除南省正郎。

translations.literal: He repeatedly submitted memorials on affairs; because his views met with approval he was soon appointed a regular director in the southern ministries.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly submitted memorials on affairs of state, and because his views met with approval he was soon appointed a regular director in the southern ministries.

sentences.zh: 天福中，承詔與張昭遠等修《唐史》，竟集其功。

translations.literal: During Tianfu he received an edict to compile the History of Tang with Zhang Zhaoyuan and others, and ultimately brought the work to completion.
translations.idiomatic: During Tianfu he received an edict to compile the History of Tang with Zhang Zhaoyuan and others, and ultimately brought the work to completion.

sentences.zh: 開運中，自兵部郎中授右諫議大夫，賞筆削之功也。

translations.literal: During Kaiyun he was transferred from Director in the Ministry of War to Right Remonstrance Grand Master, in reward for his work in literary compilation.
translations.idiomatic: During Kaiyun he was transferred from Director in the Ministry of War to Right Remonstrance Grand Master, in reward for his work on the historical compilation.

sentences.zh: 及契丹犯闕，偽旨遣使於晉州率配豪民錢幣，以實行橐。

translations.literal: When the Khitans assaulted the capital, a forged edict dispatched an envoy to Jin Prefecture to levy and apportion money from wealthy families to fill the traveling coffers.
translations.idiomatic: When the Khitans assaulted the capital, a forged edict dispatched an envoy to Jin Prefecture to levy and apportion money from wealthy families to fill the traveling coffers.

sentences.zh: 始受命之日，條制甚嚴，熙出衣冠族，性素輕急，既畏契丹峻法，乃窮理搜索，人甚苦之。

translations.literal: From the first day he received the commission the regulations were very strict. Xi came from a gentry clan and his nature was impulsive and harsh; fearing the Khitans' stern law, he searched exhaustively by every legal means, and people suffered greatly.
translations.idiomatic: From the day he received the commission the regulations were very strict. Xi came from a gentry clan and was by nature impulsive and harsh; fearing the Khitans' stern law, he searched exhaustively by every legal means, and the people suffered greatly.

sentences.zh: 及晉之三軍殺副使駱從朗，

translations.literal: When Jin's three armies killed Vice Commissioner Luo Conglang,
translations.idiomatic: When Jin's three armies killed Vice Commissioner Luo Conglang,

sentences.zh: 〈（《通鑒》：契丹以節度副使駱從朗知晉州事，大將藥可儔殺從朗。）〉

translations.literal: (Zizhi Tongjian: The Khitans appointed Vice Military Commissioner Luo Conglang to administer Jin Prefecture, and the great general Yao Kechou killed Conglang.)〉
translations.idiomatic: (Zizhi Tongjian: The Khitans appointed Vice Military Commissioner Luo Conglang to administer Jin Prefecture, and the great general Yao Kechou killed Conglang.)〉

sentences.zh: 百姓相率持仗害熙於館舍，識者傷之。

translations.literal: The common people rose together with weapons and killed Xi at his lodging; those who understood the matter lamented him.
translations.idiomatic: The common people rose together with weapons and killed Xi at his lodging, and those who understood the matter lamented his fate.

sentences.zh: 李遐，兗州人也。

translations.literal: Li Xia was a man of Yan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xia came from Yan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 少為儒，有節操。

translations.literal: He studied Confucianism in his youth and possessed integrity.
translations.idiomatic: He studied Confucianism in his youth and possessed integrity.

sentences.zh: 歷數鎮從事，及升朝，累遷尚書庫部員外郎。

translations.literal: He served as aide in several prefectures over the years; after entering court he was promoted in succession to Vice Director in the Ministry of Revenue of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He served as aide in several prefectures, and after entering court he rose in succession to Vice Director in the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 高祖即位，以皇子重乂保釐洛邑，知遐強幹有守，除為西京留守判官，使之佐理，復重其廉勤，兼委監西京左藏庫。

translations.literal: When Gaozu took the throne, the prince Chongyi was appointed to safeguard Luoyang. Knowing that Xia was forceful and steadfast, he was appointed aide to the Western Capital's commandant to assist in administration; further valuing his integrity and diligence, he was also entrusted to supervise the Western Capital's left treasury storehouse.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu took the throne, the prince Chongyi was appointed to safeguard Luoyang. Knowing that Xia was forceful and steadfast, Gaozu appointed him aide to the Western Capital commandant to assist in administration, and further valuing his integrity and diligence, also entrusted him to supervise the Western Capital's left treasury storehouse.

sentences.zh: 會張從賓作亂，使人輦取繒帛以賞群逆，遐曰：「不奉詔書，安敢承命！」

translations.literal: When Zhang Congbin raised rebellion, he sent men to cart away silk to reward the rebels. Xia said: "Without receiving an imperial edict, how dare I accept the order!"
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Congbin raised rebellion, he sent men to cart away silk to reward the rebels. Xia said, "Without an imperial edict, how dare I accept the order!"

sentences.zh: 遂為其下所害。

translations.literal: So he was killed by their subordinates.
translations.idiomatic: So he was killed by their subordinates.

sentences.zh: 高祖聞而嘆惜，賻贈加等，仍贈右諫議大夫。

translations.literal: When Gaozu heard of it he sighed in grief; funeral gifts were increased by one grade, and he was posthumously granted Right Remonstrance Grand Master.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu heard of it he sighed in grief, increased the funeral gifts by one grade, and posthumously granted him Right Remonstrance Grand Master.

sentences.zh: 其母田氏，封京兆郡太君，仍給遐所食月俸，終母餘年。

translations.literal: His mother, née Tian, was ennobled as Lady of Jingzhao Commandery; she continued to receive the monthly salary that Xia had drawn until the end of her years.
translations.idiomatic: His mother, née Tian, was ennobled as Lady of Jingzhao Commandery and continued to receive the monthly salary that Xia had drawn until the end of her life.

sentences.zh: 其子俟服闋與官。

translations.literal: His son was granted an office after his mourning period ended.
translations.idiomatic: His son was granted an office after his mourning period ended.

sentences.zh: 後又遣兗州節度使李從溫就其舊業，賜牲幣綿帛等物，以旌其忠也。

translations.literal: Later the military governor of Yan Prefecture, Li Congwen, was dispatched to attend to his old household, and sacrificial victims, ritual silks, cotton cloth, and other goods were granted to honor his loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: Later the military governor of Yan Prefecture, Li Congwen, was dispatched to attend to his old household, and sacrificial victims, ritual silks, cotton cloth, and other goods were granted to honor his loyalty.

sentences.zh: 尹玉羽，京兆長安人。

translations.literal: Yin Yuyu was a man of Chang'an in Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Yuyu came from Chang'an in Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 唐天福中，隨計京師，甚有文稱。

translations.literal: During the Tianfu era under Tang, he traveled to the capital for the metropolitan examination and enjoyed a considerable reputation for literature.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianfu era he traveled to the capital for the metropolitan examination and enjoyed a considerable reputation for literary talent.

sentences.zh: 會有苴杖之喪，累歲羸疾，冬不釋菅屨，期不變倚廬。

translations.literal: When he incurred the mourning of staff and cane, for successive years he was emaciated and ill; in winter he did not lay aside his straw sandals, and throughout the mourning period he did not leave his mourning hut.
translations.idiomatic: When he incurred the mourning of staff and cane, for years he was emaciated and ill. In winter he did not lay aside his straw sandals, and throughout the mourning period he did not leave his mourning hut.

sentences.zh: 制闋，隱居杜門，無仕宦之意。

translations.literal: When mourning ended, he lived in seclusion behind closed doors with no mind for office.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning ended, he lived in seclusion behind closed doors with no wish for office.

sentences.zh: 梁貞明中，劉鄩辟為保大軍節度判官，歷雍、汴、滑、兗從事。

translations.literal: During Zhenming under Liang, Liu Yan recruited him as military governor's aide of the Baoda army; he successively served as aide in Yong, Bian, Hua, and Yan.
translations.idiomatic: During Zhenming under Liang, Liu Yan recruited him as military governor's aide of the Baoda army, and he served in succession as aide in Yong, Bian, Hua, and Yan.

sentences.zh: 〈（案：以下有闕。

translations.literal: (Note: There is a lacuna below.
translations.idiomatic: (Note: There is a lacuna below.

sentences.zh: 考宋黎持《移石經紀》：石經舊在務本坊，自天祐中韓建築新城，而石經委棄於野。

translations.literal: Examining Song Lichi's Record of Moving the Stone Classics: The stone classics formerly stood in Wuben Ward; from Tianyou onward Han Jian built the new city wall, and the stone classics were abandoned in the wild.
translations.idiomatic: Examining Song Lichi's Record of Moving the Stone Classics: The stone classics formerly stood in Wuben Ward; from Tianyou onward Han Jian built the new city wall, and the stone classics were abandoned in the wild.

sentences.zh: 至朱梁時，劉鄩守長安，從幕吏尹玉羽之請，輦入城中，置於此地，即唐尚書省之西隅也。）〉
