translations.literal: When the Zhu Liang dynasty came, Liu Yan held Chang'an; at the request of his staff officer Yin Yuyu, the classics were carted into the city and placed at this spot, at the western corner of the Tang Department of State Affairs.)〉
translations.idiomatic: When the Later Liang came, Liu Yan held Chang'an; at the request of his staff officer Yin Yuyu, the classics were carted into the city and placed at this spot, at the western corner of the Tang Department of State Affairs.)〉

sentences.zh: 唐清泰中，為光祿少卿，退歸秦中，以林泉詩酒自樂，自號自然先生。

translations.literal: During Qingtai under Tang he served as Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices; he retired to the Qin region and found his pleasure in forests, springs, poetry, and wine, styling himself Master Ziran.
translations.idiomatic: During Qingtai under Tang he served as Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, then retired to the Qin region and found his pleasure in forests, springs, poetry, and wine, styling himself Master Ziran.

sentences.zh: 宰臣張延朗手書而召，高臥不從，謂人曰：「庶孽代宗，不可仕也。」

translations.literal: Chief Minister Zhang Yanlang summoned him by letter in his own hand, but he remained reclining and did not obey, telling others: "An illegitimate scion rules in place of the ancestral temple—one may not serve him."
translations.idiomatic: Chief Minister Zhang Yanlang summoned him by letter in his own hand, but he remained reclining and did not obey, telling others, "An illegitimate scion rules in place of the ancestral temple—one may not serve him."

sentences.zh: 及高祖入洛，即受詔而來，以所著《自然經》五卷貢之，且告其老。

translations.literal: When Gaozu entered Luoyang, he immediately accepted the summons and came, presenting his own five-volume Classic of Nature and also declaring his old age.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu entered Luoyang, he immediately accepted the summons and came, presenting his own five-volume Classic of Nature and declaring his old age.

sentences.zh: 即日璽書褒美，頒其器幣，授少府監致仕，月給俸錢及冬春二時服。

translations.literal: That very day an imperial letter of seal-script praise was issued; ritual vessels and silks were bestowed, and he was granted retirement as Vice Director of the Palace Revenues, with monthly salary stipends and clothing for winter and spring.
translations.idiomatic: That very day an imperial letter of seal-script praise was issued, ritual vessels and silks were bestowed, and he was granted retirement as Vice Director of the Palace Revenues with monthly salary stipends and clothing for winter and spring.

sentences.zh: 天福中，卒，有《武庫集》五十卷行於世。

translations.literal: During Tianfu he died; his fifty-volume Armory Collection circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: During Tianfu he died, leaving his fifty-volume Armory Collection in circulation.

sentences.zh: 鄭雲叟，本名遨，雲叟其字也，以唐明宗廟諱，故世傳其字焉，本南燕人也。

translations.literal: Zheng Yunsou, original personal name Ao—Yunsou was his courtesy name; because of the temple taboo on Mingzong of Tang, posterity transmitted his courtesy name, and he was originally a man of Southern Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Yunsou, whose original personal name was Ao and whose courtesy name was Yunsou, was originally a man of Southern Yan. Because of the temple taboo on Mingzong of Tang, posterity transmitted his courtesy name.

sentences.zh: 少好學，耿介不屈。

translations.literal: He loved learning in his youth and was upright and unyielding.
translations.idiomatic: He loved learning in his youth and was upright and unyielding.

sentences.zh: 唐昭宗朝，嘗應進士舉，不第，因欲攜妻子隱於林壑，其妻非之，不肯行，雲叟乃薄遊諸郡，獲數百緡以贍其家，辭訣而去。

translations.literal: During the reign of Emperor Zhaozong of Tang he once took the Jinshi examination but failed; he therefore wished to take his wife and children and live hidden in mountains and valleys. His wife disapproved and refused to go, so Yunsou traveled lightly through various prefectures, obtained several hundred strings of cash to support his family, bade farewell, and departed.
translations.idiomatic: During the reign of Emperor Zhaozong of Tang he once took the Jinshi examination but failed. He therefore wished to take his wife and children and live hidden in mountains and valleys, but his wife disapproved and refused to go. Yunsou then traveled lightly through various prefectures, obtained several hundred strings of cash to support his family, bade farewell, and departed.

sentences.zh: 尋入少室山，著《擬峰詩》三十六章，以導其趣，人多傳之。

translations.literal: Soon he entered Mount Shaoshi, composed thirty-six chapters of Peak-Inspired Poetry to express his inclinations, and many people copied and circulated them.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he entered Mount Shaoshi and composed thirty-six chapters of Peak-Inspired Poetry to express his inclinations, which many people copied and circulated.

sentences.zh: 後妻以書達意，勸其還家，雲叟未嘗一覽，悉投於火，其絕累如此。

translations.literal: Later his wife sent a letter expressing her wishes and urging him to return home; Yunsou never so much as read it once—he threw it all into the fire. So thorough was his severing of worldly ties.
translations.idiomatic: Later his wife sent a letter expressing her wishes and urging him to return home, but Yunsou never so much as read it—he threw it all into the fire. Such was his severing of worldly ties.

sentences.zh: 俄聞西嶽有五鬛松，淪脂千年，能去三屍，因居於華陰。

translations.literal: Soon he heard that the Western Peak had a five-needled pine that oozed resin for a thousand years and could drive out the three corpses; he therefore settled at Huayin.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he heard that the Western Peak had a five-needled pine that oozed resin for a thousand years and could drive out the three corpses, and he therefore settled at Huayin.

sentences.zh: 與李道殷、羅隱之友善，時人目為「三高士」。

translations.literal: He was on friendly terms with Li Daoyin and Luo Yin; people of the time regarded them as the "Three High Recluses."
translations.idiomatic: He was on friendly terms with Li Daoyin and Luo Yin, and people of the time regarded them as the "Three High Recluses."

sentences.zh: 道殷有釣魚之術，鉤而不餌，又能化易金石，無所不至，雲叟恒目睹其事，信而不求。

translations.literal: Daoyin possessed the art of fishing with hook but no bait, and could also transform and transmute metal and stone—there was nothing he could not do. Yunsou constantly witnessed these things and believed without seeking them for himself.
translations.idiomatic: Daoyin possessed the art of fishing with hook but no bait and could also transform and transmute metal and stone—there was nothing he could not do. Yunsou constantly witnessed these things and believed without seeking them for himself.

sentences.zh: 雲叟與梁室權臣李振善，振欲祿之，拒而不諾，及振南遷，雲叟千里徒步以省之，識者高焉。

translations.literal: Yunsou was on good terms with Li Zhen, the powerful minister of the Liang court; Zhen wished to give him an official salary, but he refused and would not agree. When Zhen moved south, Yunsou traveled a thousand li on foot to visit him—those who understood the matter held him in high esteem.
translations.idiomatic: Yunsou was on good terms with Li Zhen, the powerful minister of the Liang court. Zhen wished to give him an official salary, but Yunsou refused. When Zhen moved south, Yunsou traveled a thousand li on foot to visit him, and those who understood the matter held him in high esteem.

sentences.zh: 後妻兒繼謝，每聞兇服，一哭而止。

translations.literal: Later his wife and children died in succession; whenever he heard of mourning garments, he wept once and stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Later his wife and children died one after another; whenever he heard that someone was in mourning, he wept once and stopped.

sentences.zh: 時惟青衿二童子、一琴、一鶴，從其遊處。

translations.literal: At that time only two youths in blue collars, one zither, and one crane accompanied him in his wanderings.
translations.idiomatic: At that time only two youths in blue collars, a zither, and a crane accompanied him wherever he went.

sentences.zh: 好棋塞之戲，遇同侶則以晝繼夜，雖寒風大雪，臨檐對局，手足皸裂，亦無倦焉。

translations.literal: He loved chess and pitch-and-toss games; when he met companions he would continue from day into night, and even in bitter wind and heavy snow, sitting under the eaves facing one another across the board, his hands and feet cracked with chilblains, yet he never showed weariness.
translations.idiomatic: He loved chess and pitch-and-toss; when he found companions he would play from day into night. Even in bitter wind and heavy snow, sitting under the eaves across the board from them with cracked hands and feet, he never grew weary.

sentences.zh: 唐天成中，召拜左拾遺，不起。

translations.literal: In the Tiancheng era of Tang he was summoned and appointed Left Remonstrance Aide but did not take up the post.
translations.idiomatic: In the Tiancheng era of Tang he was summoned as Left Remonstrance Aide but declined to serve.

sentences.zh: 與羅隱之朝夕遊處，隱之以藥術取利，雲叟以山田自給，俱好酒能詩，善長嘯。

translations.literal: He spent his days and nights in company with Luo Yin; Yin made a living through pharmaceutical arts, while Yunsou supported himself with hillside fields. Both loved wine and were skilled at poetry, and excelled at long whistling.
translations.idiomatic: He spent his days with Luo Yin, who made a living through pharmaceutical arts while Yunsou supported himself from hillside fields. Both loved wine, wrote poetry well, and were skilled at long whistling.

sentences.zh: 有大瓠，雲可辟寒暑，置酒於其中，經時味不壞，日攜就花木水石之間，一酌一詠。

translations.literal: He had a large gourd that he said could ward off cold and heat; he placed wine in it and even after a long time the flavor did not spoil. Each day he carried it among flowers, trees, water, and rocks, taking a drink and composing a verse.
translations.idiomatic: He owned a large gourd that he said could ward off cold and heat; wine placed in it did not spoil even after a long time. Each day he carried it among flowers, trees, water, and rocks, drinking and composing a verse in turn.

sentences.zh: 嘗因酒酣聯句，鄭曰：「一壺天上有名物，兩個世間無事人。」

translations.literal: Once, when wine had warmed them, they composed linked verses; Zheng said: "One pot—a famous thing from heaven; two men in the world without affairs."
translations.idiomatic: Once, when they were warm with wine, they composed linked verses; Zheng said, "One pot—a famous thing from heaven; two men in the world without affairs."

sentences.zh: 羅曰：「醉卻隱之、雲叟外，不知何處是天真。」

translations.literal: Luo said: "When drunk, apart from Yin and Yunsou, I no longer know where true innocence lies."
translations.idiomatic: Luo said, "When drunk, apart from Yin and Yunsou, I no longer know where true innocence lies."

sentences.zh: 高祖即位，聞其名，遣使賫書致禮，征為右諫議大夫，雲叟稱疾不起，上表陳謝。

translations.literal: When Gaozu ascended the throne he heard of Yunsou's name and sent an envoy bearing a letter and gifts to summon him as Right Remonstrance Grand Master; Yunsou pleaded illness and did not rise, submitting a memorial to decline with thanks.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu took the throne he heard of Yunsou's fame and sent an envoy with a letter and gifts to summon him as Right Remonstrance Grand Master. Yunsou pleaded illness and declined, submitting a memorial of thanks.

sentences.zh: 高祖覽表嘉之，賜近臣傳觀，尋賜號逍遙先生，以諫議大夫致仕，月給俸祿。

translations.literal: Gaozu read the memorial and praised it, ordering it passed among his close ministers for viewing; soon he granted him the title Master Free Wanderer and allowed him to retire as Remonstrance Grand Master with a monthly salary.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu read the memorial and praised it, having it passed among his close ministers for viewing. He soon granted Yunsou the title Master Free Wanderer and allowed him to retire as Remonstrance Grand Master with a monthly salary.

sentences.zh: 雲叟好酒，嘗為《詠酒詩》千二百言，海內好名者書於縑緗，以為贈貺。

translations.literal: Yunsou loved wine and once composed an Ode to Wine of twelve hundred characters; those throughout the realm who admired his name copied it onto silk and gave it as gifts.
translations.idiomatic: Yunsou loved wine and once composed an Ode to Wine of twelve hundred characters. Admirers throughout the realm copied it onto silk and gave it as gifts.

sentences.zh: 復有越千里之外，使畫工潛寫其形容列為屏障者焉。

translations.literal: There were also those from more than a thousand li beyond Yue who sent painters to sketch his likeness secretly and array it on screens.
translations.idiomatic: Some even came from more than a thousand li beyond Yue and sent painters to sketch his likeness in secret and mount it on screens.

sentences.zh: 其為時望所重也如此。

translations.literal: Such was the esteem in which men of the age held him.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the esteem his contemporaries accorded him.

sentences.zh: 天福末，以壽終，時年七十四。

translations.literal: At the end of Tianfu he died a natural death at age seventy-four.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Tianfu he died a natural death at the age of seventy-four.

sentences.zh: 有文集二十卷行於世。

translations.literal: A collection of writings in twenty juan circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: His collected works in twenty juan circulated widely.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：自古攀龍鱗，附鳳翼，坐達於雲衢者，豈獨豐沛之士哉！

translations.literal: The historiographer says: From antiquity those who grasped dragon scales and attached themselves to phoenix wings, reaching the cloud highways while seated—were they only men of Feng and Pei!
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer says: From antiquity, those who grasped dragon scales and attached themselves to phoenix wings, rising to the highways of the clouds while still seated—were they only the men of Feng and Pei!

sentences.zh: 茍懷才抱器，適會興王，亦可以取貴於一時，如盧質而下數君子是也。

translations.literal: If one cherishes talent and bears capacity, and happens to meet a rising sovereign, one may also win honor for a time, as with Lu Zhi and the several gentlemen below him.
translations.idiomatic: If one cherishes talent and bears capacity and happens to meet a rising sovereign, one may also win honor for a time, as with Lu Zhi and the several gentlemen below him.

sentences.zh: 至如國珍之讜直，仁願之友悌，趙、李二子沒於王事，皆無忝於士林矣。

translations.literal: As for Guozhen's forthright integrity, Renyuan's fraternal devotion, and the two men Zhao and Li who perished in the service of the state—all were without shame before the community of scholars.
translations.idiomatic: As for Guozhen's forthright integrity, Renyuan's fraternal devotion, and Zhao and Li, who perished in the service of the state—all were without shame before the community of scholars.

sentences.zh: 唯玉羽之貞退，雲叟之肥遁，足可以柅奔競之風，激高尚之節也。

translations.literal: Only Yuyu's steadfast withdrawal and Yunsou's ample reclusion were sufficient to check the wind of frantic striving and inspire the integrity of the lofty-minded.
translations.idiomatic: Only Yuyu's steadfast withdrawal and Yunsou's ample reclusion were enough to check the wind of frantic striving and inspire the integrity of the lofty-minded.
